text:
Maya S.: heads up — EU customer (NL) reports 200–300ms extra tail latency and a bunch of 401s this morning. They say traces show traffic landing in us-west.
Chris P.: ugh. any dig/curl from their side?
Maya S.: pasted from customer: ```$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.redwood-inference.com
54.243.12.34
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION: udp:4096 ; EDNS: version: 0 ; flags: ; COOKIE: <redacted>
``` They also included a curl that hits us-east IP and returns 401: ```curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/ -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< x-region: us-west-2
```
Ricardo M.: that IP (54.243.12.34) is in our us-west pool. Did their resolver strip ECS or rewrite EDNS?
Chris P.: customer says their ISP runs a transparent proxy/CGN and strips EDNS-client-subnet. Without ECS the authoritative anycast might pick an upstream resolver answer that points to the wrong pop.
Maya S.: support ticket created with raw pcap + customer dig: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-5421
Support Bot: Ticket RED-5421 created and assigned to support-ops. SLA: 4h.
Janet L.: quick check: are our geoip DBs synced across edge caches? Last sync job shows eu geodb pushed 02:14 UTC but edge reported a brief 503 to S3 at 02:13. Could that cause a fallback to old mapping?
Ricardo M.: plausible but the dig shows the authoritative responded with a us IP. That means either our authoritative geoip routing returned wrong answer OR the recursive resolver is returning a cached US answer. Need to confirm TTL & AA flags.
Chris P.: asked customer for full dig +trace and the resolver's ADDITIONAL section. They sent this: ```;; QUESTION SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.com. IN A
;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood-inference.com. 300 IN A 54.243.12.34
;; Query time: 48 msec
;; SERVER: 203.0.113.9#53(203.0.113.9) (their ISP)
``` That server is an ISP resolver in NL that appears to be returning our us-west cached answer.
Maya S.: so repro likely flow: customer v6 -> ISP NAT64 proxy -> ISP resolver strips ECS -> cached US answer returned -> traffic lands in us-west -> token bound to eu token fails validation -> 401 + higher latency.
Janet L.: mitigation ideas: 1) recommend customer use 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 (if allowed) to avoid ISP cache, 2) short-term: enable geo-redirect header fallback in edge (X-Redwood-Region: eu) for EU certs, 3) ops: purge the affected record from authoritative cache and reduce TTL.
Ricardo M.: ops purge done for the nl resolver cohort and TTL lowered to 60s. Watch metrics for auth failures and cross-region egress.
Support Bot: RED-5421 updated: ops purge complete, TTL set 60s, suggested customer workaround posted.
Maya S.: customer confirmed tests via 1.1.1.1 now land in eu and 401s stopped. Leaving ticket open for root cause and long-term fix.
Chris P.: long-term: we should document ISP/CGN NAT64 signatures and add a resolver-heuristics check in our routing layer (prefer ECS answers when available, fallback to closest geoip otherwise). Also add a KB article about using public resolvers for geo-critical workloads.
Janet L.: filing follow-up RFC for geoip sync verification + adding a probe job that checks common ISP resolvers in major EU ISPs for stale answers.
Maya S.: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for monitoring thresholds in case this flares. :white_check_mark:
